data.one_liner: Records user journeys, network traffic, and errors into a self-contained HTML file.
data.what_it_does: Records the user journey in a Flutter app including screens, taps, network requests, logs, and errors. Exports the complete session as a single self-contained HTML file that can be replayed offline in any web browser.
use_when: You need to collect reproducible bug reports and session evidence from testers or users.
You want to replay user journeys offline without maintaining a dedicated backend dashboard.
avoid_when: You require real-time cloud streaming of session analytics and remote monitoring dashboards.
You are building for platforms where file sharing or local recording is restricted.
strengths: Self-contained HTML export requiring no server, account, or internet connection to view.
Captures network traffic with cURL generation, screenshots, and stack traces on a single timeline.
Built-in privacy controls like automatic password masking and RedactedZones.
weaknesses: Cloud logging and remote upload integrations are no longer included out-of-the-box.
File sharing is not supported on Linux platforms.
data.setup_notes: Initialize FlogFlow before runApp, configure navigator observers, and add companion interceptors for Dio or package:http if network capture is desired.
